clue.text: Composer 0 brood distractedly at home

indicators.note: acting distractedly, the letters of brood are thrown into disorder

parts.note: someone at home is said to be in

explanation.surface: A composer sits moping at home, unable to concentrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distractedly' rearranges BROOD into BOROD; IN for 'at home' follows. The stray '0' is a printing mark and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Borodin was the Russian who wrote Prince Igor and the Polovtsian Dances.

clue.text: Better lock bag there's a build up of work

indicators.note: to better something is to improve it by reworking, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Locking the bag up is wise when work is piling up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like a comparative but is a verb signalling the rearrangement of LOCK BAG.
explanation.definitionFit: An accumulation of tasks still to be dealt with is arrears of work.

clue.text: Torn container limits how much a letter can take

annotationWithheld.why: Torn container limits how much a letter can take (4-11): RENT for 'Torn' is clear, but 'container' cannot give RESTRICTION and no scan or reprint is available to repair what is likely an OCR garble
annotationWithheld.clue: Torn container limits how much a letter can take

clue.text: Such a food plan will make one wither with time

parts.note: to wither is to die away, as plants do

explanation.surface: A strict eating plan will make the dieter waste away in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime of controlled eating is a slimming regimen.

clue.text: Only relatively interested in good jobs?

definitions.text: Only relatively interested in good jobs?

parts.words: Only relatively interested in good jobs?
parts.note: sounds like someone lukewarm about career prospects; really it is someone keen only to hand plum posts to relatives

explanation.surface: A half-hearted job seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively' seems to mean 'somewhat' but means 'concerning relatives'.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring one's kin with posts is nepotism, and this is its adjective.

clue.text: Ready-to wear one in hospital?

definitions.meaning: to wear something is to put up with it, so someone ready to wear trouble is forbearing
a person receiving treatment on a ward

explanation.surface: A sign in a clothes shop's window muddles off-the-peg fashion with a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes 'Ready-to wear' look like off-the-peg clothes, but 'wear' here is the British sense 'tolerate', as in 'I won't wear that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbearing and long-suffering is one sense; the other is a person under a doctor's care.

clue.text: This meter takes the standard sovereign

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a king is a sovereign ruler

explanation.surface: A coin meter that accepts a gold sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' suggests the old gold coin fed into a meter, but here it is a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A street meter you feed when leaving a car is named for vehicle stopping.

clue.text: Semi-nautical order of fish

indicators.note: putting letters in a new order rearranges them
semi means half, so the first half of the word nautical is taken

explanation.surface: Fish arranged in a seafaring order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Semi' takes NAUT, half of 'nautical'; 'order of' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large oceanic food fish of the mackerel family.

clue.text: Air of white collar workers in row?

definitions.text: Air of white collar workers in row?

parts.words: Air of white collar workers in row?
parts.note: reads as the mood of office workers in a dispute; really a tune sung by schoolboys in white collars who row

explanation.surface: The atmosphere among office staff during a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white collar workers' suggests office staff and 'row' a quarrel; Eton is a famous English public school whose boys wore wide white collars and row on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The school's famous rowing song, a melody sung by its pupils.

clue.text: Former coins of driving-examiners

definitions.meaning: the tester was a sixteenth-century silver coin
people who conduct a test of a learner's driving

explanation.surface: Old coins belonging to driving examiners.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester was an old Tudor shilling, and examiners are people who test.

clue.text: Sharing same time, like Ovett and Coe -yet could be a most open Coe run

definitions.text: Sharing same time, like Ovett and Coe

indicators.note: the phrase says the following words might become something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two great British middle-distance runners of the same era, and a wide-open race for one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges A MOST OPEN COE RUN. Steve Ovett and Sebastian Coe were rival British middle-distance runners of the early 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that coincide in date are of one period, as the two athletes' careers were.

clue.text: Decoy left by the river

parts.note: the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A duck decoy is left floating beside the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoy entices prey, as bait or an enticement does.

clue.text: Second outing to Peel

parts.note: an outing is a short excursion or jaunt

explanation.surface: A second excursion to a place called Peel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peel' looks like a destination (there is a Peel on the Isle of Man), but it is the verb meaning to remove an outer layer.
explanation.definitionFit: To peel off clothing or bark is to take it off, a synonym.

clue.text: French translation of "The Little Minister"

parts.note: the title of J M Barrie's novel suggests a book being translated, but the clue asks for the French word for a minor cleric

explanation.surface: A French edition of J M Barrie's novel about a Scottish minister.
explanation.definitionFit: In France a priest or minor cleric is addressed by this title, a small-scale minister of the church.

clue.text: Mark of infamy that's hard lines, too

definitions.text: Mark of infamy that's hard lines, too

parts.words: Mark of infamy that's hard lines, too
parts.note: a burned-in sign of disgrace, which is also lines seared hard into the skin and is bad luck for the bearer

explanation.surface: A badge of disgrace is bad luck as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard lines' is British slang for bad luck; a mark burned into a criminal's skin was both disgrace and misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma burned into a criminal's flesh with a hot iron.

clue.text: Conservative, inexperienced learner-driver. Drive slowly

parts.note: raw means green or untrained
L is the plate displayed by a learner driver in Britain

explanation.surface: A cautious novice motorist takes the road slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To move at a snail's pace in traffic, as cars do in jams.

clue.text: Trouble starts with bad cigars affecting the stomach

indicators.note: bad cigars are spoiled, so their letters are spoiled into a new order
the start of the word Trouble supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: Smoking bad cigars brings stomach trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes T from 'Trouble'; 'bad' rearranges T with CIGARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric means relating to the stomach, as in gastric flu.

clue.text: Right-back among the football successes in Glasgow

indicators.note: one piece is placed among the letters of the other, inside it

parts.note: goals are what a team scores to succeed
RB is the shorthand for the right-back position on a team sheet

explanation.surface: A right-back joins the goalscorers in a Glasgow football match.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gorbals is a district of Glasgow south of the Clyde, once notorious for its slums; the definition names where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gorbals is a historic inner-city area of the Scottish city.

clue.text: High gear needed for Viscount's take-off

definitions.text: High gear needed for Viscount's take-off

parts.words: High gear needed for Viscount's take-off
parts.note: reads like a Vickers Viscount airliner needing a high gear to get airborne; really it is the headgear a viscount wears

explanation.surface: A Viscount airliner needs high gear to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Viscount was a British airliner, so 'take-off' and 'gear' suggest aviation; 'High gear' is headgear and the viscount is a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers wear a small crown of rank at coronations, each grade with its own design.

clue.text: International row, clad otherwise?

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: An international quarrel dressed up as something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges ROW CLAD; the whole clue also describes an East-West conflict fought by other means than open war.
explanation.definitionFit: The decades of hostility between the Soviet bloc and the West without direct fighting.

clue.text: Are responsible for bank accounts?

parts.note: reads as clerks in charge of accounts; it also plays on people who give accounts, that is, narrators of stories

explanation.surface: Who looks after the customers' money at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Bank cashiers handle deposits, and narrators give an account of events.

clue.text: Beginning to dry, canvas sheet getting lighter

indicators.note: the beginning of the word dry gives just its first letter

parts.note: an awning is a canvas sheet stretched over a shopfront or deck

explanation.surface: Laundry on a canvas sheet starts to dry as the sky brightens.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is when the sky grows bright, so the word describes light increasing.

clue.text: Endows college head with new seat

parts.note: a don is a senior member of a college

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters of seat are remade in another order

explanation.surface: A college head endows a new chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SEAT into ATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give money or property, a synonym for giving gifts.

clue.text: Lee and Grant, almost, provide officer material

definitions.text: Lee and Grant, almost, provide officer material

parts.words: Lee and Grant, almost, provide officer material
parts.note: two American Civil War commanders are each almost the whole pair's rank in the singular, and the word also means broad or all-purpose material

explanation.surface: Two famous American Civil War commanders as models for officers.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert E Lee and Ulysses S Grant led the Confederate and Union armies; each held this senior rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior army rank held by both commanders, and the adjective for broad, all-purpose stuff.

clue.text: Where on the canal to make fast?

definitions.meaning: the gated chamber where boats are raised or lowered

explanation.surface: A question about where on a canal a boat should be tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal has gated chambers for changing level, and to secure a door with a key is to fasten it.

clue.text: Soft pencil, very soft — paper not yet written on

parts.note: B marks a soft pencil lead, as in 2B
lank means limp and lifeless, as of hair

explanation.surface: An artist with a soft pencil and a sheet of fresh paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean sheet with nothing on it is empty, the adjective for an unmarked page.

clue.text: One drink? Not for it in the country

definitions.text: Not for it in the country

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, meaning one
gin is a common spirit

explanation.surface: A country dweller turns down a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the country' marks the answer as rural dialect: it is a country way of saying 'against'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialect for against, as in rustic speech: someone opposed to a thing is agin it.

clue.text: Trouble in orbit? It's among the worst yet seen

indicators.note: the answer lies among the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A space mission's trouble ranks among the worst yet seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orbit' suggests space but here means the eye socket, where a stye is an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A small inflamed swelling on the eyelid, an eye infection.

clue.text: Boom! Spirit messages come up 11

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: raps are knocks from spirits at a seance

explanation.surface: A seance where the spirits' knocking messages arrive with a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boom!' sounds like an exclamation but is the nautical pole. The trailing '11' is a misprint and does nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom is a ship's pole for a sail, a kind of mast or yard.

clue.text: Series of guarded political speeches run on party lines?

definitions.text: Series of guarded political speeches run on party lines?

parts.words: Series of guarded political speeches run on party lines?
parts.note: a campaign trip by train, with brief speeches at each station; the railway lines and the party line are both in play

explanation.surface: A politician campaigning carefully, sticking to the party line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run on party lines' suggests toeing the party line, but it also means a tour run along railway lines, stopping briefly at small stations.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign of quick stops at many towns, originally by train, giving short speeches at each.

clue.text: Soccer scouts?

parts.note: reads as talent spotters for football clubs; it plays on the Glasgow football club and on older members of the Guide movement

explanation.surface: Talent spotters for a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasgow's famous football club shares its name with the senior branch of the Girl Guides and with patrolling forest wardens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Glasgow club is a soccer side, and its name also means senior Guides or patrol scouts.

clue.text: " It " girls, perhaps, once employed in Roman baths

indicators.note: perhaps says the given words are one possible arrangement, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Glamorous 'It' girls once worked in Roman bath-houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges IT GIRLS. Romans oiled their skin and scraped it clean with a curved metal tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved scraper used by Roman bathers to remove oil and sweat from the skin.
